content:
Leila: Quick note — onboarding emberlite-embed on news-qa-holdout. FP16 baseline looks clean but int8 run shows recall@5 drop that's worrying.

Leila: FP16 recall@5=0.812, int8 recall@5=0.784 (single run). Precision/ndcg also ticked down a bit.

Omar: Did you change batching or padding behavior for the int8 path? Sometimes we flip to dynamic padding to save mem.

Leila: Good call. Our int8 runner used dynamic padding + batch-by-token packing. FP16 was fixed-pad to 512.

Priya: That could change microbatch composition and therefore kernel selection and KV cache behavior. Even tiny float diffs can move nearest neighbors.

Sam: Also check whether quantization calibration was per-channel symmetric or per-tensor. Per-channel usually preserves neighborhood better for embeddings.

Leila: This was per-tensor calibrate from the quick-calib script. I can re-run per-channel.

eval-bot: Job 4398765439 queued: run_embed_eval(model=emberlite-embed,int8,calib=per-tensor)

Leila: Re-ran with fixed-pad=512 + packing disabled, int8 per-tensor: recall@5=0.799 (better but not back to fp16).

Omar: OK that points to two factors: (1) dynamic padding/packing changes batching; (2) quant path per-tensor vs per-channel. Try per-channel next with fixed-pad.

Priya: Also capture per-example rank diffs. We usually store a small TSV: id,rank_fp16,rank_int8,rank_delta. That helps pinpoint if a few anchors flip a lot or it's broad noise.

Leila: Command I'm using:
```
./eval_embed \
  --model emberlite-embed \
  --dataset news-qa-holdout \
  --pad-length 512 \
  --batch-size 128 \
  --quant int8 \
  --calib-mode per_channel \
  --packing disabled \
  --save-ranks s3://redwood-evals/emberlite/v1/ranks.tsv \
```

eval-bot: Job 4398765450 started: run_embed_eval(model=emberlite-embed,int8,per_channel)

Leila: Results in: int8 per-channel + fixed-pad: recall@5=0.808, ndcg almost identical. Per-anchor TSV shows ~3.4% anchors moved by >5 positions in top-100.

Omar: That's not ideal but within expected sensitivity. For onboarding policy, do we accept int8 if recall@5 drop <= 0.5% and <=5% anchors move >5 positions?

Priya: Let's be stricter given customer SLAs. Proposed gate: recall@5 drop <=0.25% and anchor-moves >5 positions <=3%. If exceeded, mark quant profile as opt-in and add detailed notes.

Sam: Agreed. Also add deterministic eval checklist item: fixed-pad, disable packing, set RNG seed, and run n=3 seeds (42, 271828, 314159) to estimate variability.

Leila: I'll run the 3-seed sweep with per-channel int8 + fixed-pad and upload artifacts to s3://redwood-evals/emberlite/v1/seed-sweep/{umap,ranks,manifests}. Will open PR with results and recommended gating.

Omar: Could also try mixed-int8 strategy: store float-cache for long contexts or high-variance anchors. Might be overkill for now.

Priya: For the regression tests, capture a small representative query set (n=5k) and compute recall/anchor-delta; fail CI if int8 median rank delta > 2.

Leila: Uploaded initial artifacts. Linking in the onboarding PR now. s3://redwood-evals/emberlite/v1/seed-sweep/manifest.json

Sam: Nice triage. TL;DR: dynamic padding/packing + per-tensor quant amplified numeric drift. Use fixed-pad + per-channel calib + seed-sweep to validate int8.

Leila: Filing a short runbook entry in the onboarding repo: "Int8 onboarding: fixed-pad, per-channel calibrate, disable packing, seed-sweep = 3".

Priya: Thanks — please include the per-anchor TSV and a small script to compute the % anchors moving >k positions. Saves future finger-pointing. :thumbsup:

Leila: Will do.
